analysis:
Reviewed LaunchAgent.swift (head) and the LaunchAgentLifecycleTests changes (patch plus base).

Changed behavior: `kickstartIfLoaded()` (LaunchAgent.swift:188-191) now returns the result of `kickstartInPlace`, which returns Bool (lines 199-222). If launchctl reports the service vanished (exit 113, '3:' or 'could not find service') and `reloadIfMissing` is false, it returns false instead of the previous unconditional true. Because the watchdog passes `reloadIfMissing: false`, it still never reloads or resurrects a provider that the user stopped. This preserves the stop/disable semantics and the 'never revive a stopped provider' property. The new false return lets the watchdog recovery (WatchdogRecoveryService, not supplied) avoid committing a KV backend crash-loop guard trip when no restart was issued. That caller was not examined, so its handling of the new false return is unverified.

New test at LaunchAgentLifecycleTests.swift:495-670 drives the real adapter with scripted launchctl. It checks that no enable or bootstrap verbs run, the plist is unchanged, and the guard record is restored or not committed. Test-only; the launchctl runner is a task-local seam, so no production attack surface was added.

The patch excerpt for LaunchAgent.swift is truncated; the head text was reviewed in full. The status-113 and stderr-contains heuristics are loose: `stderr.contains("3:")` could match unrelated errors. This is pre-existing and only shifts whether the call returns false or throws, not authorization.

No change to attestation, encryption, authorization or serving authorization (TB-011, A-016) was found. Related T-043 (watchdog rollback) and T-041 are not materially affected. Next pass should confirm the WatchdogRecoveryService caller handles the false return and stages the guard trip atomically.
